stem: When resuscitating a bleeding child, what is the recommended approach to fluid management?

options.text: Aggressive use of isotonic crystalloids to maintain blood pressure
Early transition to blood products and limiting crystalloids
Withholding all fluids until surgery is available
Initial use of multiple colloid boluses
Repeated large crystalloid boluses until bleeding stops

explanation: Early transition to blood products and limiting crystalloids is the recommended approach in a bleeding child because it supports circulation while reducing dilutional coagulopathy, hypothermia, and worsening of trauma-related coagulopathy.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because aggressive crystalloid resuscitation is discouraged in bleeding trauma due to dilutional coagulopathy and other complications.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because early blood product administration with restricted crystalloid use helps restore circulating volume while avoiding worsening coagulopathy and hypothermia.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because fluids should not be withheld entirely; ongoing haemodynamic support is needed while definitive haemorrhage control is arranged.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because colloids are not the preferred initial strategy for bleeding resuscitation in children.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because repeated large crystalloid boluses can dilute clotting factors and worsen shock-related complications.

source.hint: Consider the risks of dilutional coagulopathy mentioned in the talk.
